title: One-Act Play
subtitle: Two pairs of eyes, locked upon the selfsame star.

trails.title: "Trash"
trails.description: "Trash" that has lost the protection of a velvet box and leather envelope.

content.text:
May 26, 1913

We can no longer pretend that nothing is happening here! The world is about to descend into chaos!

The upper echelons of the empire were indeed harboring a Russian spy. Before this, everyone regarded him as a hero of the empire, but he turned out to be a secret operative, sending his own compatriots to the enemy's guillotine. Who knows how much intelligence he has sent back to Russia? Is our country just a naked fool in the eyes of the Russians? 

The whole of Europe is secretly in turmoil, wars are breaking out everywhere—everywhere! Even in Vienna, one can always hear whisperings of war, and the people no longer have the heart or the mind to appreciate art. The bullets of war have shattered the glass domes of Vienna, the sound of shattering echoes through the nights of beautiful dreams, scratching the phonograph records, and clogging the tubes of the horn.

Is tonight the last time I will sit in the opera house? Oh, beautiful place, like a mother's womb, only here can my grief and panic about the war be alleviated. Perhaps I should transfer my family fortune, but where to? Or should I exchange it for gold bars and jewels, and hide them in a secret compartment under my bed? It was only two short years ago! How wonderful it was then—there was no constant call to war between nations, and mankind was as innocent as Adam and Eve before they left the Garden of Eden ... No ... No ... I shouldn't make such comparisons. I do not wish to face a fate of eternal damnation.

Perhaps all this is just baseless speculation on my part. Perhaps I have been infected by those madmen who fantasize about the end of days. Now, there are few countries that even come close to the Austro-Hungarian Empire, and I cannot imagine scenes of war ravaging Vienna any time soon. Such a scene would indeed herald the end of the entire world ...

*A fine leather notebook! An expensive gold-plated pen! What's that embossed on its velvet box ...? "Fischer"?

*The good parts have already been ripped off! D**n it! Just leave this broken book in the trash!

items.text: One-Act Play

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Feeling better now? Is anything still haunting you, talking to you?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Do you remember who you are, Isolde?
The clinic returns to silence as Kakania holds Isolde's hand, observing with concern the pale actress before her.
She looks toward the tabletop mirror, allowing tears to fall from her hollow eyes.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Oh, yes, doctor. I see it now.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: That fire, the fire that devoured everything! How could I ever forget?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The raging fire consumed everything, including Theophil. He was screaming—his mind was already gone before he ignited it all.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: How could he ignore everything with such disregard? Who allowed him to forget with such disregard?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: While I remember, I remember it all. I'm from a noble family, I need to be a qualified Dittarsdorf, an outstanding arcanist, a first-rate opera singer, a good sister, and a good daughter ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Never forget my manners, never forget the family!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: But he—he got away with it! If Theophil was truly a man of courage, he should've joined the army, or fought a duel with someone—that would've made his death more honorable!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yet, he chose to die this way, after a life of debauchery.
She breathes a heavy and bitter sigh, and finally, color returns to her face.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *sobs* I'm sorry ... I shouldn't have told you that.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's okay, Isolde, you're doing it right. That's what therapy is for.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: These memories are exactly what we need. What's been deliberately repressed and ignored in the depths of your heart will manifest into words, and help you reconnect with your emotions. Soon your symptoms of hysteria will diminish!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't be afraid. You can talk to me about anything. In the name of my family and the Hippocratic Oath, I will keep things between you and me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Everything will be a secret, our secret.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Our secret ...
The woman's cheeks, still wet with tears, reveal a tragic smile, like dew on rose petals.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Sounds wonderful.
She closes her eyes, striving in that moment to open them without being free from the fog of the past.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I remember that room.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The room was excessively bright. I never got used to light bulbs, preferring the softer light of candles. My mother always had a white candle burning when she saw me at bedtime.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What happened to that candle?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Someone knocked it over. Ha! That naughty brat, my dark-haired brother!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He lit the candle, set the room on fire, and burned all his paintings!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He ran to me, his body burning! In his hand was ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: A gun.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I once told Theophil, he's not a genius like Weininger. Biting the bullet won't make him famous. Only a debut leaves an impression, the shows that follow are boring repetitions.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He laughed. "Indeed. Too many have shot themselves for fame. Only through passionate fire would the world remember me."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I bid him farewell, and went downstairs to talk to the ladies. Blood soaked the wooden floor and dripped into my cup. Plop, plop, plop. I went upstairs and found Theophil lying in a pool of blood.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: A revolver was in his hand. Ah, how its cylinder clicked like music.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I lifted my dress so the fire could roll down like water. I leaned over to the hole on his left temple and said, "Theophil, where is your fire?"

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Theophil sat up, and said, "Isolde, where's your gun?"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Your gun?"

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... My gun?
Her voice trailed out into a low sinister growl.
Isolde swoons toward her reflection in the mirror, her hand raised high as if delivering a monologue on stage.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: My gun! I remember now, I was holding the gun all along!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Theophil stood in the study. The flames engulfed the beam, the ceiling, everything.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What?!
Kakania speaks as softly as possible despite her shock, with the intent not to disturb the woman's soliloquy.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He ran toward me, screaming, in pain. He was burning, the heat drying up my eyes ...
The woman begins to shake under the weight of revelation.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He was on fire, and running towards me. Doctor, he ran at me!
She clenches her teeth, trying to squeeze out words, gripping her chest as if to squeeze out her insides—to open herself like a finely crafted wooden box, offering herself to her rescuer.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Breathe in, breathe out ... It's okay, Isolde. I'm here by your side. You're safe.
Kakania extends her arms, gently encircling the woman into her embrace.
She breathes deeply, calming down inside the green warmth.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And then, I heard a shot.
Their embrace tightens slightly.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I-I can't remember ... The trigger was hard to pull. After the shot, it slipped out of my hand ...
She lifts her head up towards the good doctor, tears flowing from her eyes.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I killed Theophil! It was me!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I don't deserve the right to attend his funeral, or to hold his memorial art exhibit. I don't deserve any of the sympathy and kindness ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I should have burned in that fire, I should have died! *sobbing*

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's fine.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm neither judge nor police, Isolde. I'm just your doctor. I'll remain faithful to you, no matter what you think you are.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Your life was in danger. Anyone would've done the same.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It was not your fault, Isolde. You were just ... terrified.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't be ashamed of your instinctive behavior. Rest assured, your secret is safe with me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: According to Dr. Freud, embracing your darkness is the first step to liberation.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It takes courage, and is not easy to do. Most people can't do it, but you've done a very good job.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I did a good job?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes. An excellent job.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor ...
Her tears now are like a broken dam, relieved of the burden that it had too long held.
Kakania holds her gently, waiting for her long-overdue catharsis to come to an end.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Alright, this is as far as I can walk you. You have to host a ceremony tomorrow, and Tosca's next week. Vienna won't forgive me if I take up too much of your time.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Don't worry about it. Like you said, the night breeze will do me some good.
She still cleaves hard to Kakania's arm, imperceptibly shaking her head.
As twilight falls, few passersby notice the distinguished opera singer among them.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I heard from Heinrich that you're trying new things?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I read his stage design. The style of Berlin expressionism he adopted is quite refreshing.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have to admit, he became a little strange after his trip to Berlin. But his passion for art didn't change, nor did his love for his fellow Viennese.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I appreciate his hard work as well. But sadly, the Vienna Court Opera didn't approve our performance application, so we turned to the Vienna People's Opera.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Well, I'm not surprised. Understand that Mr. Mahler is the artistic director of the Vienna Court Opera, and even he could not bring Salome to the stage.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Those boring, stale old-timers will never approve of new forms of art. They always expect something predictable and unvarying, the same old pieces and settings.
Her complexion darkens again as she turns her head.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I'm the reason Tosca can't get the permission.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Because I, the star, am a medium, a maniacal "arcanist."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, no, that's not it. In Vienna, the great composers, conductors, and performers ... almost all of them have been arcanists.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Wiping out the unique talents of arcanists and their artistic contributions would be like setting fire to the cultural tapestry of Viennese society!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, sorry. A flood! A flood is better ...
The actress is, or at least acts, oblivious to this minor slip.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: They consider it a desecration of the stage. When a singer is channeling, she's essentially asking a spirit to possess her and speak directly through her, thus she "becomes" the character in the opera ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: People will question the authenticity of the voice—is this still the singer's own voice? Or is it fraud?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No, Isolde. They think that, because they know nothing about performance, not even the slightest thing.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The nature of the stage is to be someone else. If they're so intent on the presentation of the true self, the mirrors in my clinic would like a word with them.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It is an actor's job to become another person. On stage, in a fictional world, they briefly trick our eyes into thinking it's real.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And to achieve that, we rehearse rigorously, through sweat and pain. We take care of the music, the costumes, the settings, the lights ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Your gift helps you do this better than others. That's all.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: But I used the arcane skills of the Dittarsdorf family. I couldn't have done these things without them.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: What if an arcanist's talent for art is also a curse?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Maybe I'm just a fraud, doctor. I'm propped up by my illness, and once it's cured, my talent will be gone with it ...
Kakania pauses abruptly.
She turns back, looking at an operatic genius tormented by her own talents.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's not like that, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Using your talents is not cheating.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We're "arcanists." But before we allow ourselves to be defined by that word, who are we really?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If an "arcanist" grew up on a lonely island, she wouldn't see herself as an "arcanist," but as a "person" like you, like me, like everyone.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor ...
Isolde meets her gaze as the stars twinkle back in Kakania's eyes.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But you know, the truth is, when I look at a crowd, I don't see any "arcanists"!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All I see is our people, with different talents, trapped in life, their selfhoods ground smooth until they're indistinguishable from the crowd.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Humans celebrate their flaws, yet they persecute our gifts.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: They control the narrative. They define our gifts as diseases, our talents as weaknesses, and our bloodlines as curses.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If we're cured, we're just another face in the crowd. But if we live on with our "diseases," we're forever ill, forever afflicted.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We arcanists have to live in such a world, where we survive through suffering.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at this city, this most enlightened, tolerant city. Under the sweet surface of the Sachertorte lies powder and poisonous wine.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Arcanists are recognized for their artistic abilities, nothing more. We hold no parliamentary seats, no professional titles, and no professional credentials.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We are exiled and marginalized. Our only voice in the culture is to be decoration, because decoration impacts nothing.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The restrictions and discrimination against arcanists are worsening by day. First we had to register with the government, then we needed residence permits, and now, permission to cast arcane skills.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And we can do nothing but tolerate, stay polite and dignified. Be a "good" arcanist, show no signs of "instability," because we're supposed to stay rational, otherwise, we're animals.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But people are complicated, they can't stay rational forever—as Dr. Freud said, we're just seeing the tip of the iceberg.
As the streetlights come on, Kakania looks up, now resembling an actress mid-monologue beneath the stark light.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You might be sick, I might be too. But the truth is, this whole society is sick! You can't just treat the individual and ignore the bigger picture.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It was the repression of irrational desires that allowed the diseases to spread in our time.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In this case, the people on that island are much freer than we are!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You mean that mysterious island? I hear gold is in the ground there.
Kakania nods with vigor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Remember the lady from the Foundation?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yes. Why?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: She said the arcanists on that island are not lunatics, and they're living a life free of restrictions.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Doesn't that sound great? If we could form our own society, like those artistic associations, and have control over our own production and labor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This must've been some kind of enlightenment. I can almost see it, they'll show us another way of life, a kingdom free of repression.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: To help them is to help ourselves. And that's also what your exhibit is about.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Me? No, I'm not as great a person as you.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But you are working for a great cause.
The stars in her eyes begin to spread out. Kakania reveals a deep and tender smile.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde, my friend. I've shared my dream with you, and I hope one day it'll become your own, until the day when everyone shares the same dream.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Our society needs a revolution, a radical surgery.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We urgently need a new vision to reunite us at the dawn of the new century.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Like the secession in art history, we need a secession of arcanum to distinguish us from "hysterical lunatics," "street peddlers," and "con artists."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We need a new dream, a new saga. We need to reinvent ourselves and become a new people.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No more repression, only the full embrace of our primal desires.
Kakania concludes her monologue, removing her hat to fastidiously straighten the feathers on top.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's why your work has not been in vain! From Theophil's art exhibition to the promotion of new art ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Do not doubt yourself. You're helping a great cause.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Thank you, doctor. This is the first time anyone's said that to me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I will bear that in mind.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Your words in the breeze of night have been stirring. Can you walk with me a little longer?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I'd like to hear more things about the secession you mentioned, so that I can prepare my speech for tomorrow's ceremony ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes. It is my pleasure.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Would you like a walk to the Vienna People's Opera? I think they put up new posters.
TO BE CONTINUED…
